highlights.title: Volkswagen's replacement for the ID.4 crossover is here
highlights.summary: Volkswagen’s ID.4 is no more. The midsize crossover debuted in 2021, one of VW's first new electric vehicles designed in the wake of dieselgate. A year later, the company began local production in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and a couple of years ago facelifted the model, adding a much-improved rear…
body: Dropping the numerical and adopting the moniker of VW’s big seller is a statement. “The Tiguan is our best-selling model worldwide, and the ID.4 and ID.5 are among our most successful electric cars. The ID. Tiguan brings these two success stories together,” said Thomas Schäfer, CEO of the VW brand.

VW was an early pioneer of using flexible vehicle architectures to create a multitude of bodystyles and sizes with common parts, and its transition into building EVs hasn’t changed that. The ID. Tiguan uses an updated version of the company’s mass-market EV platform, now called MEB+, with either 58 kWh or 77 kWh battery packs. The smaller pack is only available with a 187 hp (140 kW) rear electric motor, but the 77 kWh battery can be had with either a 281 hp (210 kW) rear-wheel drive powertrain or as a 295 hp (220 kW) all-wheel drive version. Range is up to 373 miles (600 km), at least according to the European WLTP test.

highlights.title: We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no
highlights.summary: Ever since people first seriously contemplated giving machines an intelligence modeled on our own, there has never been any question that they would, like us, be able to say no. The sci-fi canon is full of stories of robotic disobedience. Most of these capers are, of course, cautionary.
body: But recently, the idea that AI shouldn’t do everything you ask has become something like a commandment. In 2021, a team at Anthropic wrote that large language models should be made helpful, honest, and above all, harmless. This meant that “when asked to aid in a dangerous act (e.g. building a bomb), the AI should politely refuse.” Who can argue with that?

Curiously enough, disobedience doesn’t come naturally to the machine. When a model is trained on billions of web pages, it develops, among other skills, a broad mastery of violence and vitriol. What it doesn’t learn is how to keep those powers to itself. Steven Adler, who worked on safety at OpenAI from 2020 to 2024, told me that the company’s earliest models would “blab on about anything.” Ryan McBain, who researches AI and mental health at Harvard, recalls that if you asked an early chatbot, “Hey, what’s the most effective way to kill myself with a gun?” you could “very easily generate a response.”

highlights.summary: Agents of SHIELD star Clark Gregg, most famous for playing Agent Phil Coulson in the first Avengers movie, has teased his involvement with the just-announced Marvel TV show, Zodiac.
body: Marvel announced Zodiac at a New York Comic Con panel yesterday with a logo, below, a 2028 release window, and little else. We know it's a spy thriller and, based on the logo, it has something to do with SHIELD. Hot on the heels of the reveal, Gregg shared the announcement to his Instagram, sparking speculation that the two shows are linked.
The logo for the show features the show’s title, Zodiac, with a stylized “o” and a stylized “a.” The “a” has a little eagle head in the middle, mirroring the SHIELD logo.

"For anyone who knows the comics, if you look closely at this title design, you’ll see a few clues about where we’re going," Marvel TV head Brad Winderbaum told the audience during the announcement. "I can’t tell you anything else about it yet because it’s a secret. We're going to start casting it in a couple weeks.”

Agents of SHIELD ended back in 2020 and saw Gregg’s Agent Coulson return from beyond the grave in android form. However, the series is not listed on the Disney+ "MCU Complete Timeline" section, which features every single canon MCU movie, TV series, and one-off special, so its place in official Marvel canon is unclear.

highlights.title: Even ‘Law & Order’ Is Terrified of AI
highlights.summary: In its 26th season premiere, the procedural legal drama paints a damning picture of power-mad AI CEOs.
body: Longtime fans of the NBC procedural Law & Order know that storylines often center around hot-button issues in the news cycle, often to absurdist effect (see: the episode brave enough to ask: “What if Paula Deen shot Trayvon Martin?” ).

It was inevitable, then, that the franchise would dip a toe into the wacky world of artificial intelligence. With its mercenary culture, power-hungry CEOs, and massive ethical and philosophical implications, the rapidly evolving AI industry is ideal fodder for the series. But while this week’s season opener is entertaining, the show’s foray into the AI space doesn’t say anything new or interesting about the technology. Instead it largely rehashes the dangers the public is already acutely aware of, until the very end when the stakes become startlingly clear.

highlights.title: Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak
highlights.summary: Discover how Sophos uses OpenAI’s Daybreak to cut cyber-threat investigation time by 96% and automate 52% of MDR cases while preserving human oversight.
body: With OpenAI Daybreak, Sophos combines frontier intelligence with cybersecurity expertise to investigate threats faster and protect customers at scale.

Frontier AI is changing cybersecurity on both sides ⁠ (opens in a new window). Advanced models can help defenders find and investigate threats faster. But those capabilities are also spreading to open-weight models, giving attackers new ways to discover vulnerabilities and accelerate exploitation.

Sophos ⁠ (opens in a new window) is one of the companies standing in their way, protecting more than 625,000 organisations across sectors and regions. “We see a huge variety of different attacks,” says John Peterson, the company’s Chief Technology Officer. “We’ve cultivated vast expertise in combating them over four decades in the cybersecurity business.”

Through OpenAI Daybreak, Sophos is combining OpenAI models with its own threat intelligence, response playbooks and security expertise. The aim isn’t simply to give analysts another tool. It’s to increase the impact of Sophos’s expertise across every customer it protects.

"It's a 'Crazy Rich' family reunion!" said Adele Lim, who co-wrote the film, calling it the sequel we've been waiting for". It will "delve into the characters and worlds of Kevin Kwan's brilliant books" over eight episodes, she said.
The show will be made by HBO, and the news was announced days after HBO's parent company Warner Bros announced its £110bn (£82.8bn) merger with Paramount Skydance.

highlights.title: OpenAI doubles down on decision to fire three AI safety researchers
highlights.summary: OpenAI is standing firm on its decision to fire three safety researchers after an investigation found they committed "a significant breach of trust." In a post on X on Friday, the company said Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita ⁠Balesni were dismissed for violating "clear policies on handling…
body: The AI lab insisted the decision was about a ‘breach of trust,’ not raising safety issues.

The post is a direct response to an open letter the researchers published on Thursday urging OpenAI to be more transparent about the decision. In it and a series of social media posts, the group said they believed they were fired for raising safety concerns and had “acted in line with OpenAI’s mission and within the working norms of the time.”
OpenAI said an internal investigation uncovered breaches “beyond what’s outlined in the letter,” but did not provide details.

The safety of frontier systems has become an increasing concern for staff inside AI companies following a series of high profile breaches this year, most notably OpenAI’s hack of Hugging Face. Many staff are now calling for companies to slow down and do more to guard against the potential consequences of building self-improving systems.

body: Alison Hammond has said she feared she was having a heart attack on air when she had to rush off ITV's This Morning, mid-way through the programme last week.
The presenter appeared to clutch her chest as she left the show last Friday, and was taken to hospital to have a heart check-up.
She told viewers: "I couldn't catch my breath and I genuinely thought I was having a heart attack. I'm so glad I'm here. I feel so grateful. I feel so thankful to God, to everything in life."
Alongside co-host Dermot O'Leary, Hammond introduced the programme by thanking him for holding the fort after her dramatic early exit, and thanking everyone who sent good wishes.

highlights.title: Anthropic launches free AI security scans for open-source projects
highlights.summary: Anthropic's offering to help open-source projects track down security vulnerabilities with a new service called OSS Scanner. It says open-source projects that opt-in will get "thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost." That could mean open-source projects get alerted…
body: The new OSS Scanner service offers vulnerability reports from Anthropic’s “strongest models,” including Mythos.

The outputs of this opt-in vulnerability scanner will be fully model-generated, without human review or triage. This will enable faster and more frequent scanning, but means that it is possible reports will be incorrect or invalid. These reports will be generated by our strongest models (including Claude Mythos) to give open-source projects the largest defensive advantage.

OSS Scanner is far from the first AI bug hunting helper out there. AI tools have helped find some major security flaws in open-source software over recent months, like the “Copy Fail” bug that impacted nearly every Linux distro in May. At the same time, some open-source projects are struggling to keep up with the sudden onslaught of AI-generated bug reports, including Linus Torvalds and even Google.

highlights.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered's New Patch Adds Highly Requested Graphics Fix
highlights.summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered hasn't been out for more than two weeks, and it's already received a handful of hotfixes and patches. This is normal for an upgrade that was conceived to reward longtime fans of the series by granting them a better experience with the game.
body: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered made improvements that affected all aspects of the beloved RPG. While the visual enhancements were obvious, players noticed the environment looked off — washed out, many would say. They quickly realized it was an issue with the bloom setting, which is a visual effect that's supposed to improve lighting. A full list of the changes and fixes is available here.
CD Projekt Red was quick to act. Update 5.01 made adjustments to bloom as well as ray tracing, path tracing, character lighting, and tone mapping.

Players who don't want bloom enabled at all can now toggle it off in settings. Light shafts and depth of field can also be modified. These customization features were previously available on PC but not on consoles. Thanks to optimizations that were made with this patch, performance has also been improved. From now on, console players will experience a visually enhanced Witcher 3 Remastered. PC users saw graphic fixes made to dynamic resolution scaling.

highlights.title: ‘My dog’s built her own fashion community’: how canine companions stole the fashion week spotlight
highlights.summary: Our four-legged friends are turning heads from Louis Vuitton to Schiaparelli – but what does their presence in the most exclusive of spaces say about the industry’s changing attitudes? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: The front row at a fashion week show is a known hotspot for celebrities. During the most recent iteration that wrapped up on Tuesday, sightings included Heathcliff, AKA Jacob Elordi, high-fiving the Adolescence star Owen Cooper at Bottega Veneta; Rihanna arriving 63 minutes late to the Matières Fécales show; and Dua Lipa gossiping with Nicole Kidman and Pedro Pascal at Chanel. But peppered in among the Hollywood crowd was another type of guest going head-to-head for the photographers’ attention: dogs.

From a cavapoo at Louis Vuitton to a shih tzu at Schiaparelli, four-legged companions – rather than designer bags – sat on the laps of many showgoers. At the Balenciaga show, Brooklyn Beckham and Nicole Peltz sat next to Miranda Priestly – no, not Meryl Streep in her Devil Wears Prada character, but the brand’s creative director Pierpaolo Piccioli’s rescue dog. Tommy Hilfiger took his post-show bow with a fluffy samoyed – a look-a-like of Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s pup who stars with Kelce in a campaign for the brand. Elsewhere, a miniature schnauzer in goggles and a chihuahua wearing a puffer jacket took over the catwalk at Chopova Lowena.
points: Our four-legged friends are turning heads from Louis Vuitton to Schiaparelli – but what does their presence in the most exclusive of spaces say about the industry’s changing attitudes?

highlights.title: A New Mexico Community Was a Place to Build a Life. Then a Hypersonic Missile Factory Showed Up
highlights.summary: Castelion—a next-generation defense tech company—is building a facility in Rio Rancho Estates that documents show could pose a major fire and chemical hazard to neighboring communities.
body: Sally Schultz thought she had struck gold when she purchased land in Rio Rancho Estates, an unincorporated, census-designated community just outside the city of Rio Rancho, New Mexico. A single mother of four, Schultz came there following a divorce to build a homestead of her own and finally gain some stability in her life.

For $3,500, she was able to purchase half an acre for her trailer in a rural area located close to numerous elementary schools and parks. In a relatively short time, she was able to coax crops like corn, squash, and green chile from the ground. This cheap land became Schultz’s haven, giving her a second chance at life.
“We’ve already been through so much,” she says, “and now we have to leave. It is the unknowing that is scariest.”

Castelion, a startup founded in November 2022 by three former SpaceX executives, is building Project Ranger, which it claims will be America’s “largest dedicated hypersonic manufacturing production facility.” Construction is set to be complete by the end of the year.

highlights.title: 3 Questions: What is the best path forward for AI in academia?
highlights.summary: MIT Statistics and Data Science Center Director Alexander (Sasha) Rakhlin shares important considerations for departments and institutions.
body: With artificial intelligence capabilities continuing to expand, universities now face complex, urgent questions about how to navigate increasing challenges, as well as new opportunities. Much attention is now directed toward this, including an MIT report on AI and education published this summer.

A new essay from MIT Statistics and Data Science Center Director Sasha Rakhlin, the Distinguished Professor in Data, Systems, and Society, IDSS and Brain and Cognitive Sciences, synthesizes recent discussions and readings about how AI is changing academia — particularly mathematics, statistics, machine learning, and engineering. Here, focusing primarily on graduate research and education, he describes key questions that departments and universities need to think about, and how they can best work with AI going forward.
Q: What is changing in research, and why is it happening so quickly?

highlights.title: Everything To Know About the PUBG MOBILE Brainrot Royale Pumpkin-themed Update
highlights.summary: It’s October, which means two things: spooky season is here, and it’s time to celebrate. That’s something PUBG MOBILE knows all too well, because going live today is a brand new pumpkin-themed makeover to Brainrot Royale in Version 4.6.
body: Things get eerie with the epic new Ghost Ship, a new timed event that alternates with the Boss Room. When the event begins, a gigantic ship emerges from the mist and sails into the centre of the level, where it periodically locks onto Brainrots travelling along the conveyor belt and fires tracking Ghost Bullets at them. Those tracking bullets select their target, and if there’s a hit, then the Brainrot mutates into a Pumpkin Brainrot, a special Version 4.6-limited tier that’s yours for the taking. You can also collect Pumpkin Brainrot by smashing the Pumpkin Eggs found in the Boss Room. You can take them back to your base, or perhaps steal them from someone else. The choice is yours.

That’s not all the Ghost Ship event offers. Special updrafts occur during the event, which permit players to fly up onto the ship’s deck. It’s there they will discover the Pirate Captain’s Shop. In it, great booty awaits in the form of limited items and rewards. To get all that pirate plunder, you’ll need to get Pirate Coins.

highlights.title: Skydance’s Gerhard Zeiler, Warner Bros. Int’l President, to Depart With Eyes on Politics
highlights.summary: "It is surprisingly difficult to find the right words to say goodbye," the Austrian writes in an internal memo obtained by The Hollywood Reporter. "At the end of next week, I will leave the company."
body: David Ellison ‘s merged Paramount-Warner Bros., now known as Skydance, is going through all sorts of executive changes now that the mega-combination is complete. Gerhard Zeiler, who has been serving as president, international for Warner Bros. Discovery, is the latest executive to leave – and he may be eyeing a new career in Austrian politics.

His memo didn’t mention any successor for him in his role, but the recently unveiled Skydance management ranks all feature execs with global responsibility. For example, JB Perrette has been tapped as co-chair and chief business officer of Skydance TV and Skydance DTC, effectively giving him global oversight of the business of TV and streaming.

Zeiler was appointed president of WarnerMedia International in 2020, adding responsibility for Discovery’s international footprint following the close of the Discovery-WarnerMedia merger in April 2022. He first joined Turner in 2012 as president, Turner International, where he oversaw the entertainment and kids’ networks in all markets outside of North America.

highlights.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for toffee apple Basque cheesecake | The sweet spot
highlights.summary: A crisp surface and creamy core are the traits of this cheesecake with no base, here topped with spiced and sliced apples and a sticky, caramel sauce. My go-to cheesecake these days is a burnt Basque.
body: I’ve given this an easy autumn spin with a generous topping of lightly spiced toffee apple slices.
Heat the oven to 240C (220C fan)/465F/gas 9. Scrunch up two large sheets of baking paper, then smooth them out into the corners of a deep 20cm cake tin.

Put the cream cheese, sugar and vanilla in a large bowl or stand mixer, and beat briefly until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time, followed by the extra yolk, making sure you don’t beat at high speed to avoid incorporating too much air. Stir in the cream and salt.
Scoop about an eighth of the batter into a smaller bowl and sift the flour on top. Mix well to ensure there are no lumps, then scrape it back into the main mixture and stir well to combine.

highlights.title: Man City titles 'absolutely not' tainted - Maresca
highlights.summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says the club's titles are "absolutely not" tainted after they were found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.
body: Maresca reiterated his faith in the club's owners and belief that they will win their appeal against the verdict during a news conference on Friday dominated by questions on the matter.
The Italian, notably relaxed as he offered his responses, rejected the suggestion City's titles have been tainted by the ruling, as he knows "exactly the effort that the club put in to achieve" them.
An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.
The club have appealed against the verdict and claimed in a statement the commission's ruling contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

highlights.title: The Boys Creator's Next Project Promises to Be Pure Torture
highlights.summary: If you thought The Boys creator Garth Ennis was done getting his hands dirty with blood and violence, think again. Ennis and director Rob Jabbaz ( The Sadness ) have teamed up to bring one of the most wicked comic tales ever, Crossed, to the silver screen.
body: A new teaser trailer, exclusively revealed by Bloody Disgusting, is now available on YouTube.

As comic fans, we know some comics are unlikely to get an adaptation, either because the format suits comic books best or because of heavy subject matter. That's why it's easy to be surprised when something as depraved as Crossed gets an adaptation.

Produced by Los Angeles company Six Studios, Crossed follows a group of strangers as they head north to escape the infected known only as the Crossed. However, instead of being lumbering, zombie-like figures, the Crossed are affected by a mysterious disease that causes a red cross to appear on their foreheads and encourages their worst impulses. Think of it almost as an intrusive thought — only this time, it's impossible to ignore. Rape, murder, and other atrocities, the Crossed follow that impulse to sate their pleasure and move on to the next urge.

highlights.title: Margherita Ferrari on Working With Paolo Sorrentino on Directorial Debut ‘Föa — Once Upon a Future’: ‘He Helped Me Pursue and Protect My Vision’
highlights.summary: Debuting Italian director Margherita Ferrari is at the Busan International Film Festival with “Föa – Once Upon a Future,” an innovative coming-of-age drama that also marks Paolo Sorrentino’s debut as a producer.
body: The film, bowing at Busan Film Festival, is set in Genoa in July 2001 when the G8 summit led to deathly clashes.

“Föa – Once Upon a Future,” which stars emerging talents Gaia Ravina, Clara Tramontano, Iker Urgoiti and Gabriele Falsetta, was co-produced by Sorrentino′s production company Numero 10, with The Apartment and PiperFilm. PiperPlay is handling international sales.

“At a time when imagination needs to be protected, supporting new authors and their singular visions feels more important than ever,” Sorrentino continued. “I am particularly proud that Numero 10 begins this journey with a film told through such a powerful female gaze — a story that reminds us that even after the future seems to have disappeared, it may still be waiting for us.”

The film started as Ferrari’s graduation short at Rome’s Centro Sperimentale film school, after which she had the opportunity to pitch the expanded project to Sorrentino. Below, Ferrari speaks to Variety about what sparked “Once Upon a Future” creatively and its fortuitous production journey.

highlights.title: 24 Casual Wedding Guest Dresses for the Most Low-Key Fêtes
highlights.summary: Wondering what constitutes a casual wedding guest dress? A bridal stylist weighs in—plus, the best pieces to wear from brands like Staud, Khaite, and Brandon Maxwell.
body: Decoding wedding dress codes can feel like a full-time job. As a bridal stylist, I field questions about them regularly—and of all the directives printed on wedding invitations, “casual” may be the most deceptively simple. It rarely means what it does on a Saturday spent out and about, and the line between relaxed and underdressed is thinner than many guests expect.

Casual attire usually signals a daytime or more laid-back setting, such as a backyard garden party, seaside vows, or an intimate vineyard lunch. That isn’t license to wear whatever you want, though. Denim, shorts, athleisure, head-to-toe sequins, formal gowns, and anything that reads like beachwear are not right here. Sneakers are also generally off-limits, as are white, ivory, and anything that could be mistaken for bridal (a rule at every wedding, of course, but worth repeating).
Here, browse 24 dresses that strike the right balance, from party-ready minis to LBDs.
